target_customer: Startups and tech companies wanting live metrics on office wall screens
problem: Teams had key metrics scattered across Google Analytics, Twitter, Zendesk and others, with no simple live display for big screens.
product_category: real-time business dashboards and data visualization

founders.name: Rajiv Ghanta
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO by TechCrunch (2014) and the YC page. Background not found.

founders.name: Lionel Jingles
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page and in TechCrunch 2010.

founders.name: Jyotindra Vasudeo
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page and in TechCrunch 2010.

competitors.name: Geckoboard
competitors.what: Hosted dashboards for large screens pulling data from web services

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrations with several third party APIs plus a real-time display layer. Standard engineering for a small team in 2010.

defensibility.rationale: Geckoboard offered the same concept in 2010 and API integrations were easy to copy. Customers could switch dashboards cheaply.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No large incumbent copied it. AppDirect acquired the company in November 2014 to give its customers app dashboards.

market_need_then: Ambient wall displays of company metrics were an emerging practice among startups in 2010. TechCrunch noted early customers including YC, WePay and Cloudkick.

branding.domain_note: leftronic.com is now a tech statistics site, apparently under different use; current ownership not found.
branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found beyond one TechCrunch launch article and acquisition coverage.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand coverage found; known mainly through YC and two TechCrunch pieces.

outcome_analysis: Leftronic stayed small, raising about 500 thousand dollars in total per TechCrunch, and sold to AppDirect in November 2014 about four years after launch. The price was not disclosed, and AppDirect said it would keep Leftronic as a subsidiary to power customer dashboards. The record shows a modest outcome with no public growth metrics, and details on why it sold are not public.
notes: The $500K total is reported by TechCrunch 2014 and listed on Wellfound and Seedtable; the round date is not stated, so none is recorded. Investor names come from Wellfound only and are unverified. The company website now shows an unrelated tech statistics site, so the original site is effectively dead.
